data.cultural_impact: The name Astamihir holds significant cultural importance in Hindu society due to its association with the sage Astamihir from the Mahabharata. Astamihir was a great sage who was known to possess eight precious treasures, which included wealth, knowledge, food, administration, virtue, strength, pleasure, and learning. This name signifies the esteem and value placed on these wealths in Hindu culture.
data.spiritual_significance: Astamihir is a name rich in spiritual significance. It symbolizes the pursuit and attainment of material and spiritual wealth. The eight treasures referred to in the name represent the various aspects of human life - wealth, knowledge, food, administration, virtue, strength, pleasure, and learning. This name serves as a reminder of the importance of nurturing and enhancing all these aspects of life to lead a fulfilling and enlightened life. Moreover, it exemplifies the Hindu belief that true wealth lies not in material possessions but in inner peace, wisdom, and virtue.

historical_references.reference: Astamihir was a great king of the Vatsa dynasty in the 5th century BCE. He ruled over a large part of ancient India including parts of present-day Uttar Pradesh and Bihar. Astamihir is best known for his victory over the powerful King Maharaja of Magadha, which established Vatsa dominance in the region.
historical_references.context: Ancient India, Vatsa Dynasty, King of Magadha, Victory

historical_references.reference: Astamihir is also mentioned in Jain literature as a patron of Jainism. He is said to have funded the construction of several Jain temples and provided land grants to Jain monks during his reign. This further solidified his position as a powerful and benevolent king.
